To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transition of humanity to a new stage of its historical development - the stage of the "knowledge society", is accompanied by the emergence of a new type of labor - the "creative labor" of the "knowledge worker".

the transition from a labor-intensive to a knowledge-intensive economy is inevitable, but this transition can be made either painlessly or painfully, depending on whether it is accompanied by the formation of a functional alternative to work, or whether it is accompanied, as it was in the past, the formation of a labor market.

the process of digitalization of the economy and the labor market, as well as the development of automation and robotization, can lead to a situation where the traditional form of work, which is currently the main factor in social reproduction, will be completely destroyed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the negative consequences of the scientific and technological revolution, which is currently unfolding, and with the search for ways to overcome them.
the question of the possibility of a transition to the "knowledge society".

the analysis of the negative effects of scientific and technical progress, the search for effective functional and institutional mechanisms to mitigate these negative effects, the formation of a knowledge economy as a new economic system that will be capable of overcoming the negative effects of the scientific and technological revolution, and the formation of an effective functional and institutional mechanism to mitigate these negative consequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of a global economy, the problem of the future of work, as a factor of the social reproduction process, is the most urgent of all the problems of the present day.

, in order to prevent the catastrophic consequences of the negative effects of scientific and technical progress, we must urgently develop a new economic model of society, based on a new functional division of labor and a new social contract.
the process of socialization of labor is not a threat to society, but, on the contrary, it is a prerequisite for its survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the main goal of the project is to develop the mechanisms of the knowledge economy, which will allow us to overcome the threats of the digitalization, automation, robotization and the destruction of work.

it is necessary to create an effective alternative to labor in the traditional sense in the form of a system of social services, which would be provided by the state and financed from the profits of the digital economy, which would be the result of the introduction of digitalization, automation, and robotization in the global economy.
it is necessary to create a system of social guarantees for the transition of society to the post-work era.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the transition to a knowledge economy, which has been going on for decades, will be completed in the near future and will lead to a complete replacement of labor by capital and knowledge as the main factor of production.
the development of the "knowledge society" will be possible only on the basis of the transition to the "knowledge economy."
it is possible to overcome the negative impact of digitalization, automation, and robotization on the process of social production and reproduction.
